chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mūsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn —

He said: I wrote to him asking him about the bier of the deceased when it is carried: does it have a [particular] side from among its four sides that should be started with in the carrying, or is whatever is easiest for the man [sufficient], so he may carry from whichever side he wishes?
So he (the Imam) wrote back: 'From whichever [side] he wishes.'

The correct interpretation of this narration is that it lifts the prohibition on carrying the funeral bier from any of its sides, because what we have previously mentioned [of the specific method] is of the sunnah (recommended), not the obligatory.

key_terms.الْمَسْنُونِ: the recommended (sunnah); an act meriting reward if performed but incurring no sin if omitted
key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضِ: the obligatory (fard); a legally binding duty whose omission incurs sin
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْحَظْرِ: removal of prohibition; a jurisprudential principle indicating that an act is permissible
key_terms.سَرِيرِ الْمَيِّتِ: the funeral bier; the wooden frame on which the deceased is placed for transport to burial

ai.seo_question: Is there a specific side from which the funeral bier must be lifted when carrying it in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Al-Ḥusayn sent a written question (maktūba) to an Imam asking whether there is a prescribed side from which one must begin lifting a funeral bier when carrying it, or whether any side is permissible. The Imam replied permitting any side. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī then provides his interpretive commentary (wajh), reconciling this with earlier narrations specifying a preferred method by stating that starting from a specific side is a sunnah recommendation, not a legally binding obligation (fard).
